field_id_lesson.look_here_first: Start with the relatively short, much-branched dock and its widely spreading fruiting branches. Check basal leaves for a constriction above the often heart-shaped base (a 'fiddle' outline, but not every leaf shows it). Confirm on mature fruits: three expanded inner tepals ('valves') with marginal teeth and conspicuous, often warty tubercles. Leaf shape alone is not diagnostic.
measured_field_characters: Stems commonly 20–60 cm tall (occasionally about 70 cm); basal leaf blades typically 4–10 cm long, sometimes to 15 cm (Flora of North America key).
Inflorescence branches often spread roughly 60–90° from the main axis; compare the narrower 30–45° branches often seen in broadleaf dock, Rumex obtusifolius (Flora of North America key).
Mature inner fruiting tepals ('valves') about 4 mm long in the UT Austin description, with 2–5 projecting teeth per margin, to about 1.6 mm long. Measure intact mature valves with a millimeter scale.
Mature enclosed achenes three-angled and approximately 2–2.3 mm long in the UT Austin description; fruiting-valve teeth are not the achene itself.
At stem nodes, check for an ocrea: a papery sheath characteristic of Polygonaceae; it supports dock identification but is not species-specific.

local_look_alikes.separate_by: Usually longer, narrow leaves with strongly crisped/wavy margins; mature inner fruiting valves generally have entire or nearly entire margins, not the obvious marginal teeth of fiddle dock. Do not rely on leaves alone.

Generally taller with larger basal leaves (often 20–40 cm); inflorescence branches more ascending, and mature fruiting-valve tubercles typically smoother. Compare mature valves and whole-plant branching.
Also has toothed fruiting valves, so tooth presence alone is insufficient; often annual/biennial rather than perennial. Compare basal leaf form, branch architecture, and fully mature valves.

diagnostic_photo_handoff.role: Whole plant with basal leaves and widely spreading branches
diagnostic_photo_handoff.instructions: Include a ruler or recognizable scale; capture the branching angle and leaf-base outline.

diagnostic_photo_handoff.role: Basal leaf and petiole with ocrea at a stem node
diagnostic_photo_handoff.instructions: Capture leaf constriction and sheath clearly; avoid calling every leaf fiddle-shaped.

diagnostic_photo_handoff.role: Mature fruiting valves face and side views
diagnostic_photo_handoff.instructions: Photograph 2–5 marginal teeth per side where present, warty tubercles, and a millimeter scale.

diagnostic_photo_handoff.role: Dissected mature fruit with three-angled achene
diagnostic_photo_handoff.instructions: Show achene separate from persistent valves with scale.
